title: Restarts and retentive memory
summary: Tell a warm restart from a cold restart and a memory reset, and keep exactly the data that must survive a start.
objectives: Predict what warm and cold starts do to each variable
Declare retentive variables with VAR RETAIN and initial values
Check a restart in the online variable detail and the diagnostic buffer

sections.heading: Two kinds of start
sections.body: A **warm start** keeps retentive variables and initializes everything else; a **cold start** initializes everything. STOP to RUN and a warm restart start warm; a download, a memory reset and a cold restart lead to a cold start.

sections.heading: What each start keeps
sections.body: Read the table row by row.
sections.diagram:
retentive (VAR RETAIN)   other variables   function blocks
  warm start          kept                     initial value     start again
  cold start          initial value            initial value     start again
  memory reset        initial value            initial value     start again

sections.heading: Declaring retention
sections.body: Put a variable into `VAR RETAIN` to keep it over a warm start: `VAR RETAIN Count : INT := 0; END_VAR`. The initializer `:= 0` is the value both starts use when they initialize it. Inputs, outputs and function block instances cannot be retentive in PLC Lab.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body: A part counter counts 2 parts. After a warm restart the retentive Count is still 2, the next part makes it 3. After a cold restart Count is 0 again: a new shift. The diagnostic buffer shows a warm start with one retentive variable kept, then a cold start.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Declaring the CTU instance retentive to keep its count. Blocks start again on every start in PLC Lab; copy the count into a retentive variable or count with an INT.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.body: Open the retentive counter exercise, make the count survive a warm restart and check that a cold restart starts a new shift.

checkpoint.question: A variable is declared in VAR RETAIN with := 5 and has the value 9. What is it after a warm restart, and after a cold restart?
checkpoint.explanation: A warm start keeps a retentive variable; a cold start gives it its initial value 5.

checkpoint.question: Which operation never downloads the changes you made in the editor?
checkpoint.explanation: A restart uses the program and configuration already in the CPU.
